reason: The muscle-development signals are pictured acting on developing cells, matching the first goal.
expectation: The signals will guide some cells toward making muscle proteins.

alternatives.reason: The supporting-cell signals also match a goal, so either pathway seems like a reasonable place to start.

effect: The signals produced young muscle cells with messages from active muscle genes, but they do not yet have the fibre bundles.
reaction: It is interesting that the cells keep the same chromosomes while using different genes.
reason: The cells have messages for muscle proteins, and amino acids are the protein building blocks described earlier.
expectation: The young muscle cells will use the building blocks to make muscle proteins.

alternatives.reason: I could start the other development pathway first.

effect: The young muscle cells made protein bundles, completing the muscle-cell goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the messages lead to visible protein bundles.
reason: The supporting-cell signals are shown acting on another group of unspecialized cells, matching the remaining goal.
expectation: The signals will guide some cells toward becoming supporting cells.

effect: The signals produced young supporting cells with messages for support proteins, but no surrounding fibre network yet.
reaction: This looks similar to the muscle-cell pathway.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, so they may help these cells make the fibres, as they helped the muscle cells make proteins.
expectation: The cells will make support proteins and develop a surrounding fibre network.

effect: The supporting cells used the building blocks to make material around themselves, completing the remaining goal. This contrasts with the muscle cells keeping protein bundles inside.
reaction: The contrast helped make the two pathways feel distinct, though their steps were quite similar.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the muscle protein bundles was worthwhile because it connected active genes and their messages to a visible change in the cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: The supporting-cell pathway felt somewhat repetitive after the muscle pathway, even though the final result was different.

surprise.text: I was interested that cells with the same chromosomes could use different genes and end up making proteins for different jobs.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the signals matched the goals, and the amino acids were identified as protein building blocks.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how these different cells contribute to tissues and organs, although I hope the next chapter offers more varied decisions.
